title: Checkout and cashiers
summary: How paying customers works in Supermarket Simulator: customers queue at your checkout, you scan their shopping yourself, and later a hired cashier or a self-checkout can serve them.
body: At the start you are the cashier. Customers bring their shopping to the checkout and you scan each item, then take payment. Customers leave once their basket is paid for.

Who is on the till is a state rather than a fixed post. A cashier can be idle, can restock and can drop an empty box, which is why the same worker is not always standing at the register when there is nothing to scan.
Later the shop grows into hired staff and self-checkout machines. The game has separate handling for a cashier-run checkout and for a self-checkout that can need repairs.
What this entry does not tell you: wages, scan speed, patience timers or repair costs. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A checkout can be operated by a hired cashier.
Finishing a checkout is a distinct step in the game's own logic.
Self-checkout machines can break down and need repairing.
Checkout positions can be picked up and moved.
A cashier works through states of its own, including being idle, restocking and dropping an empty box.
The build names the checkout's own counter, drawer and belt grid.
facts.evidence: asset names: Checkout Counter, Checkout Drawer, Checkout Belt Grid

facts.claim: Basket icons are shipped with the checkout artwork, including a newer one.
The till itself is named: the build ships a cash register with an open and a close state of its own, in three register models.
facts.evidence: asset names: Cash Register, Cash Register Open, Cash Register Close, SM_CashRegister_A, SM_CashRegister_B, SM_CashRegister_C

facts.claim: The shop's point-of-sale terminal is named as an object of its own, with a material of its own.
The baskets and bags themselves are named in kinds: a plastic basket, two shopping bags, an old basket and a concrete basket.
facts.evidence: asset names: M_PlasticBasket, M_ShoppingBag, M_ShoppingBag2, M_old_basket, M_concrete_basket

facts.claim: The checkout furniture is textured by the build itself, with two counter sheets and a mirrored one for the self-checkout.
The build also ships a mirrored checkout counter of its own.
